learn.hook: Have you ever tried to count the stars? How far did you get before you lost count?
points: The lesson 'Chanda Mama Counts the Stars' is an imaginative story about the Moon trying to count the stars.
'Chanda Mama' is a loving name that many Indian children use for the Moon.
In this kind of story, the Moon and stars act like people. That is imagination!
Look for numbers in a story. They help you understand what happened.

example.q:
Read our story:
One night, Chanda Mama decided to count all the stars. 'One, two, three...' he began. At ten, a little star giggled and hopped to another spot. 'Oh no! Now I must start again!' said Chanda Mama. He counted to twenty, but a cloud floated by and hid five stars. Chanda Mama laughed. 'Some things are too many to count, but they are lovely to look at!'
Why did Chanda Mama have to start counting again?
steps: A little star giggled and hopped to another spot.
When a star moves, you lose track, so he had to start again.
example.answer: Because a little star hopped to another spot, and he lost count.

learn.reallife: On a clear night away from city lights, you can see many more stars. Try counting them with your family!

games.title: Story order
games.prompt: Put the star story in order
items: Chanda Mama began to count the stars.
A little star giggled and hopped away.
Chanda Mama had to start again.

games.title: True or false? (about our story)
items: Chanda Mama wanted to count the stars.
The story says he 'decided to count all the stars'.
A big cloud giggled and hopped away.
It was a little star that giggled and hopped.
The story says a cloud 'hid five stars'.
Chanda Mama got angry and cried.
In this story, the Moon talks like a person.
Chanda Mama speaks, so it is a make-believe story.

quiz.q: The story says: 'Chanda Mama decided to count all the stars.' What did Chanda Mama want to do?
quiz.explain: The first sentence tells us he wanted to count all the stars.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the first sentence

quiz.q: 'At ten, a little star giggled and hopped to another spot.' At which number did the star giggle?
quiz.explain: The story says 'At ten'.
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the numbers in the story

quiz.q: 'At ten, a little star giggled and hopped to another spot.' What did the little star do?
options: giggled and hopped to another spot
quiz.explain: The little star giggled and hopped to another spot.
quiz.mistake: Mixed up what the star did with what the cloud did

quiz.q: A star hopped away, and Chanda Mama said, 'Now I must start again!' Why did he have to start again?
options: because a star moved and he lost count
because he liked the number one
quiz.explain: When the star moved, he could not tell which stars he had counted.
quiz.mistake: Did not connect the star moving with losing count

quiz.q: 'He counted to twenty, but a cloud floated by and hid five stars.' What hid the stars?
quiz.explain: The story says a cloud floated by and hid them.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the sentence carefully

quiz.q: Chanda Mama counted 20 stars. Then a cloud hid 5 of them. How many of those stars could he still see?
quiz.explain: 20 take away the 5 hidden stars leaves 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: At the end, Chanda Mama says, 'Some things are too many to count, but they are lovely to look at!' What does he mean?
options: He will never look at the stars again.
We can enjoy things even if we cannot count them.
quiz.explain: He learnt that the stars are lovely to look at, even if there are too many to count.
quiz.mistake: Did not understand Chanda Mama's last words

quiz.q: 'A little star giggled.' What does 'giggled' mean?
options: laughed in a light, silly way
quiz.explain: To giggle is to laugh in a light, silly way.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'giggle'

teach.ask: Gappu tries to count the stars and gets mixed up. He asks: 'What happened when Chanda Mama counted the stars?'
teach.praise: Too many stars to count, but so lovely to look at! I agree, Chanda Mama!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what Chanda Mama tried to do and what went wrong?

learn.hook: One, two, three... can you spell all the way to twenty?
points: Numbers can be written as words: 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five.
Tricky spellings: eight (8), twelve (12), fifteen (15), forty (40).
13 to 19 end in -teen: thirteen, fourteen, nineteen.
Tens end in -ty: twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.
First, second and third tell us the order or position of things.
learn.reallife: When you read a big score aloud, like 'forty runs' in a cricket match, you use number words.

games.title: Match the number to its word
Smallest to largest
games.prompt: Put these number words from smallest to largest

quiz.q: Which is the correct spelling of 4?
quiz.explain: 4 is spelt f-o-u-r. 'for' and 'fore' sound the same but are different words.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up words that sound the same

quiz.q: What is 12 in words?
quiz.explain: 12 is 'twelve'. 'Twenty' is 20.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up twelve and twenty

quiz.q: Which is the correct spelling of 40?
quiz.explain: 40 is spelt 'forty', without a 'u', even though 4 is 'four'.
quiz.mistake: Adds a 'u' because 4 is spelt 'four'

quiz.q: What is 8 in words?
quiz.explain: 8 is spelt e-i-g-h-t.
quiz.mistake: Writes the word the way it sounds

quiz.q: What number is 'nineteen'?
quiz.explain: 'nineteen' is nine + teen, which is 19.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up nineteen and ninety

quiz.q: What comes next? ten, eleven, ___
quiz.explain: After 10 and 11 comes 12, which is twelve.
quiz.mistake: Skips a number

quiz.q: Five stars are in a row. The star in position 3 is the ___ star.
quiz.explain: Position 3 is 'third'.
quiz.mistake: Uses the counting word instead of the position word

quiz.q: Which is the correct spelling of 15?
quiz.explain: 15 is spelt 'fifteen', not 'fiveteen'.
quiz.mistake: Writes 'five' inside the word

teach.ask: Gappu counted 40 seeds and wrote 'fourty'. He asks: 'Did I spell it right? How do I spell numbers?'
teach.praise: Forty, not fourty! I will write it correctly now!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me how to spell forty and how the teen numbers end?

learn.hook: Can the Moon really count? No! But in our imagination, anything can happen!
points: Real things can really happen: stars twinkle, clouds float, birds fly.
Make-believe things happen only in our imagination: a moon that counts, a star that giggles.
To imagine means to make a picture in your mind.
We can use imagination to describe things in a new way: 'The stars are diamonds on a dark blue cloth.'

example.q: Is this real or imagination? 'The cloud played hide and seek with the stars.'
steps: Clouds can float in front of stars and hide them. That part is real.
But clouds cannot play games on purpose.
So the sentence uses imagination to describe something real in a fun way.
example.answer: Imagination: clouds cannot really play games.

learn.reallife: When you draw a flying elephant or make up a bedtime story, you are using your imagination!

games.title: Real or imagination?
items: the Moon goes around the Earth
a teddy bear drives a car

items.text: I closed my eyes and ___ I was flying.
A story that is not real is ___.
The full moon looked like a big silver ___.

quiz.q: Which of these can happen only in imagination?
quiz.explain: The Moon cannot count. The others can really happen.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything in the sky is make-believe

quiz.q: Which of these is real?
options: The Moon goes around the Earth.
quiz.explain: The Moon really goes around the Earth. The others are make-believe.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up real facts with make-believe

quiz.q: What do we call a story with a talking moon and giggling stars?
quiz.explain: Talking moons and giggling stars are not real, so it is make-believe.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every story is true

quiz.q: Many Indian children call the Moon by a loving name. What is it?
quiz.explain: 'Chanda Mama' is a loving name for the Moon.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Moon with the Sun or clouds

quiz.q: Which sentence uses imagination to describe the stars?
options: The stars are diamonds on a dark blue cloth.
There are many stars in the sky.
We can see stars at night.
quiz.explain: Stars are not really diamonds. Imagination helps us describe them in a new way.
quiz.mistake: Picks a plain fact

quiz.q: What does 'imagine' mean?
options: to make a picture in your mind
quiz.explain: When we imagine, we make a picture in our mind.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'imagine'

quiz.q: Which word means the same as 'make-believe'?
quiz.explain: Make-believe and pretend both mean not real.
quiz.mistake: Picks the opposite of make-believe

quiz.q: 'The Moon smiled at me through my window.' Is this real or imagination?
quiz.explain: The Moon cannot really smile. This is imagination.
quiz.mistake: Takes a fun sentence as a real fact

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Can the Moon really count? What is imagination?'
teach.praise: So the Moon can count only in my imagination! I love make-believe!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me the difference between real and imagination?
